newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Aviastar sees first jet for Kato Jan 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Aviastar sees first jet for Kato Jan 1997.

text.p: Russian plane maker AO Aviastar, optimistic about a big order which could rescue it from disaster, hopes to deliver its first Rolls Royce powered Tupolev-204 passenger jet by the middle of next year.
Tupolev chief designer Lev Lanovsky said the plane, ordered by Egypt's Kato Group, would be produced in January and delivered in April or May after certification.
"We do not have any obstacles in the work," he said.

The Kato Group, which is diversifying into aviation, has said it will buy up to 200 Tu-204s powered by Rolls-Royce engines and with U.S. Honeywell-Allied Signal's avionics in a deal which the Middle East Economic Digest says is worth $450 million.

"This contract may help Aviastar to survive and to work normally," Lanovsky said. He said the Ulyanovsk plant in central Russia has the capacity to produce 40-50 aircraft a year, but it built just five this year.
Russian officials would not confirm the cost of the deal. But Aviastar sells Tu-204 planes for $30 million each, compared to $55-$60 million for a Boeing 757.
The first part of the order will be for 30 planes, and Kato is seeking a Russian government guarantee that its cash advance will be returned if the planes are not delivered.
Lanovsky said the Russian government had promised to provide financial guarantees to the Egyptian company. "We hope it will be in next few days," he said.
Kato's president Ibraghim Kamel told Itar-Tass news agency last week that his company had placed firm orders for 30 210-seat Tu-204s and options for 170 more for delivery in 2001.
Kato plans to market the medium-haul jets in Russia and other former Soviet republics, in China and in the Middle East.
Lanovsky said Aviastar could begin supplying jets regularly from next July.
Aviastar faced serious financial problems earlier this year, including an enforced 10-week stoppage during which 28,000 workers were sent on leave.
